Again managed to "talk" to someone on the phone, given a prescription to pick-up (like in the olden days!) and told to make an appointment.
Of course, the prescription was 1/3 of what I requested, and I am using this medication for longer than my Doctor is alive, and told at reception to call at 08:00am for the appointment.
They're still using the COVID-era emergency to cut down on visits, I guess (but still get NHS money, though!).
Put in cue and forgotten if one has the energy and determination to repeat the process over and over again.
In case of death, I imagine, that the exonerating excuse would be that the patient did not use the Hospital for emergencies.
Last time I managed to see anyone with a written list of symptoms, I was told to split it up in chunks and book an appointment for each.
But, if I the skill to weave out what the symptom means, I would not need to see the Doctor expert advise... in the first place.
Unfortunately, for people that have no (reasonable) choice of using something less conductive to premature demise, there is no really solution.
In an area of heavy immigration, there is an understanding that fewer people will have the ability to complain, so le saga goes on and on

When one tries, there is a forever "try tomorrow".
Like all the rest of the other NHS surgeries of this God forgotten part of the world, their webpages is misleading.
Receptionists are not particularly rude but simply put, there are too many patients and too few doctors.
They're using the phone in morning trick as an excuse to limit the number of patients while keeping on registering new ones.
The worse part is that no one admit the crisis and effectively leave this area (certainly this surgery footprint) with a fictitious semblance of medical care.
